articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: Terry Kahl shares his positive experience from the 1996 Mt. Lassen Star Party, emphasizing the benefits of dark skies and reserved campsites in the beautiful volcanic park. His account details a group excursion to the Hat Creek Radio Observatory where they learned about the BIMA array, and his personal achievement of hiking to Lassen Peak. Kahl expresses his eagerness to return for the 1997 event.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines an activities calendar for October and November, featuring multiple star parties at various parks like Houge, Fremont Peak, Henry Coe, and Grant Ranch. It also lists general meetings, an observational astronomy class, and a reminder about Daylight Saving Time ending. Contact information for the SJAA Hotline and their homepage URL are provided for further details.

articles.title: Streaking Perseids Over the Bristlecone Pines
articles.summary: Ernie Piini recounts his experience observing the Perseid Meteor shower from the dark skies of Grandview campgrounds in the White Mountain Range, near ancient bristlecone pines. On August 11, he spotted 51 Perseids and 21 other meteors over five hours, noting the beautiful dark sky background. Despite attempts at astrophotography with a wide-angle lens, he failed to capture any meteor streaks, humorously attributing it to Murphy's Law and recommending multiple cameras for better success.

articles.title: Perseids, continued from page 1
articles.summary: The article recounts a trip to the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest in White Mountain, where the author filmed a TV program, attended a star party featuring Comet Hale-Bopp, and interviewed astrophotographer Monsignor Ronald Royer. It extensively details the scientific significance of bristlecone pines, explaining their role in dendrochronology for calibrating Carbon-14 dating and accurately determining the age of ancient artifacts and monuments like Stonehenge. The piece concludes with practical travel information and recommendations for visiting this unique natural area.

articles.title: New Event: Dark Sky Star Party at Houge Park October 4,1996 Bill O'Shaughnessy
articles.summary: Bill O'Shaughnessy announced a new Dark Sky Star Party scheduled for October 4, 1996, at Houge Park. This event aims to provide an opportunity for observers to showcase deep-sky objects like nebulae and Comet Hale-Bopp, with the organizer hoping it will become a regular occurrence alongside existing public star parties.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The document is a periodical publication statement for "SJAA Ephemeris," the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It confirms the newsletter is published 12 times a year, from January through December, and provides the association's physical address. The referenced issue is from October 1996.

articles.title: Knife-Edge Focusing for Astrophotography
articles.summary: This article introduces knife-edge focusing as a highly reliable method for achieving optimal focus in astrophotography, specifically when using telescopes. The author, Chuck Vaughn, affirms its effectiveness based on personal experience and indicates a separate article will cover focusing techniques for camera lenses.

articles.title: What's the Idea Here?
articles.summary: This article explains the basic principle and practical application of knife-edge focusing for telescopes, specifically using a Ronchi screen. It details a step-by-step procedure to achieve precise focus by adjusting the telescope until a disk of light, initially showing multiple lines, gradually reduces to a single wide line and then an evenly grayed out field at the exact focus point. The technique involves observing the movement of lines as focus is adjusted, with opposite movement indicating over-focus.

articles.title: An Imperfect World
articles.summary: This article discusses the challenges of achieving precise focus in a telescope, highlighting how factors like less than ideal seeing and imperfect optics can complicate the process. It advises observers to find the best focus by moving back and forth around the focus point. The article also explains how a telescope's f-ratio affects the criticalness and depth of focus, with faster f-ratios demanding more precise focusing.

articles.title: Some Practical Aspects
articles.summary: This article discusses practical methods for setting up and verifying knife-edge focusing on a telescope, emphasizing the precise placement of the Ronchi screen or knife-edge at the film plane. It suggests purchasing commercial focusers but also offers advice for DIY construction and provides a technique to check the accuracy of commercial devices using a camera as a reference.

articles.title: Some Final Thoughts
articles.summary: The article's first section details knife-edge focusing as a qualitative method to assess telescope optics for flaws and recommends checking focus frequently. The second, larger section is a request from author Phil Harrington for amateur astronomers to participate in the 'STAR WARE 2' survey, gathering feedback on telescopes and inviting submissions of homemade astronomy projects for a revised edition of his book.

articles.title: STRANGE BUT TRUE...
articles.summary: This article recounts a series of bizarre and unfortunate incidents experienced by an amateur astronomer named Daniel during a crowded summer observing session at Fremont Peak, including a dog attack, a squirrel startling him, and a terrifying encounter with a hummingbird. These 'unnerving' events made him reluctant to return to the site. The article also briefly describes an enjoyable public star party at Lassen Volcanic Park, noting observations and practical tips.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - Oct 1996
articles.summary: This document is a celestial calendar for October 1996, providing detailed astronomical data for observers. It includes lunar phases, planetary positions (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and SOL) with their magnitudes, distances, rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension and Declination coordinates. Additionally, it offers information on astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' for optimal stargazing.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides updates on various comets, including Hale-Bopp and Machholz 1, and reports on the recent discoveries of Comet Tabur and Comet 1996 R1. It also discusses two intriguing objects that blur the lines between comets and asteroids: 1996 PW with its comet-like orbit but asteroid appearance, and P/1996 N2 (Elst-Pizarro), an asteroid now exhibiting cometary activity. The author, Don Machholz, also notes reaching 6,000 hours of visual comet hunting.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for several comets, including C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), C/1996 N1 (Brewington), C/1996 Q1 (Tabur), C/1996 E1 (NEAT), and 96P/Machholz 1. For each comet, it lists their Right Ascension (R.A.), Declination (Dec), Elongation (EL), and estimated Sky Magnitude (SkyMag) for various dates in late 2000, aiding observers in locating these celestial objects.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a table of orbital elements for several comets, including Hale-Bopp, Brewington, NEAT, Tabur, and Machholz 1. It provides detailed astronomical parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period for each object. This data was published in the SJAA EPHEMERIS in October 1996.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document presents a series of classified advertisements for used astronomical equipment. Listings include various telescopes such as Newtonian reflectors, Celestron 5, Astro-Physics APO, and a Schmidt Camera, along with several equatorial mounts and accessories. Prices and contact details are provided for sellers, with one ad seeking a specific 10-inch Coulter telescope.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This document outlines the current status of a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes, their borrowers, and due dates, along with available units and special notes like a waiting list or a need for an operator for a specific scope. Additionally, it features classified advertisements for used astronomical equipment such as controllers, eyepieces, complete telescopes, and accessories, and provides instructions for submitting new ads.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors, including the President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and multiple Directors, along with their respective contact numbers. It also identifies an editor and is noted as part of the 'SJAA EPHEMERIS' from October 1996.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships at $15 for adults and $6 for juniors. It also offers an optional Sky & Telescope subscription for an additional $27. The form provides instructions for payment via check payable to "SJAA" and submission either in person at a meeting or by mail to the treasurer.
